newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end down on fund liquidation, cash tone.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end down on fund liquidation, cash tone.

text.p: Technical fund long liquidation and expectations of weaker cash markets pushed CME hog futures to two week lows and prices finished weaker. Pork bellies followed with concern over weakening cash belly prices and large kills adding to losses, traders said.
December paced the setback in hog futures as active fund selling added to pressure from weak cash hog values. The charts are starting to turn technically weak, traders said.
"The is the first indication of a technical downtrend," said Julia Bussie, analyst for AG Edwards, who cited a lower low on the daily charts.
Technicians also noted that December failed to post a new contract high Wednesday, when October set a new high, and then finished the day lower.
Pit sources cited active selling by ASK division of Shatkin Arbor and FIMAT Futures USA on the break.

Weaker than expected cash hog markets and concern pork product values may not be as strong as reported added to overall weakness. Slaughter rates were running fairly large and interest for pork was showing signs of easing after recent strong demand. This resulted in steady to lower cash indications for hogs Friday, traders said.

After the close, USDA confirmed trade talk by reporting Thursday's hog slaughter at 371,000 head, well above the high end of analysts' estimates. It also revised Wednesday's slaughter up to 363,000 head from 355,000 estimated Wednesday which put the weekly total at 1.446 million head versus 1.389 million in the same period last year.
"The trade fears that slaughter numbers will start to stay consistently large out here" in the corn belt, said Don Roose, President of U.S. Commodities Inc.
Roose noted that slaughter had been running large in the beginning of the week and then eased off later in the week.

Weaker-than-expected cash belly prices weighed on pork belly futures and the increased kills will likely keep marketing pipelines filled and pressure futures Friday. Cash belly prices had not hit a near-term low as expected by now, and the larger kills may be the reason, traders said.
USDA reported cash bellies steady to $2 per cwt lower at noon and traders had been looking for steady to $1 lower.

Hog futures closed 0.800 cent a lb lower to 0.425 higher with only thinly traded distant lean contracts up. December was off most at 56.700 cents. Bellies ended off 1.025 to 0.450 with February off most at 77.500 cents a lb.
